finding.claim: When header-based auth is enabled, checkUserFromHeaders copies the client-supplied HTTP header `provider` into AuthenticatedUser.Provider with no allowlist. A caller who sends `provider: system` alongside a valid username header gets Provider == "system", so executor.IsSystemExecution returns true and the 'justification required' control is skipped. The same header also lets a non-guest user be treated as a system principal.
finding.source: HTTP request header `provider` (client-controlled unless the fronting proxy strips it). This only applies when AuthHttpHeaderUsername is configured, so that Username is non-empty and runAuthChain accepts the user.
finding.sink: api_justification.go justificationProvided / validateJustificationRequired: `strings.TrimSpace(justification) != "" || executor.IsSystemExecution(user)` lets StartAction and StartActionAndWait proceed with an empty justification.

trace.note: getHeaderKeyOrEmpty(Header, "provider") is assigned to u.Provider unconditionally
runAuthChain returns the header user as soon as Username != ""; Provider is never validated
IsSystemExecution returns true when Provider == "system" and Username != "guest"
justificationProvided short-circuits to true for system executions
StartAction calls validateJustificationRequired with the user built from the headers

finding.guards_checked: The Provider value is not checked against a set of known providers. No other auth-chain element overwrites it, because the header check runs first and returns early. ACL checks use Username and Usergroup, not Provider, so only the justification requirement is bypassed. The executor ACL still applies.

finding.claim: RestartAction loads another user's execution log entry by tracking ID and re-runs it with that entry's stored Arguments and Justification. It never checks that the caller may view logs (IsAllowedLogs) for that entry. It also skips checkDashboardAccess, unlike ExecutionStatus, GetLogs and KillAction (KillAction does check IsAllowedKill). A caller with exec permission but no log permission can therefore replay a stored argument set and justification they are not allowed to see.
finding.source: RestartActionRequest.ExecutionTrackingId. Tracking IDs are UUIDs, but they can be client-chosen via StartAction's UniqueTrackingId and they appear in event streams and logs.
finding.sink: api.executor.ExecRequest with Arguments: copyStringMap(execReqLogEntry.Arguments) and Justification: execReqLogEntry.Justification, run as the caller's authenticated user

trace.note: restartActionLogEntry only checks that the entry, binding and action exist (lines 1676-1690)
validateRestartLogEntry only checks that the justification and arguments are complete (api_log_arguments.go:49-59)
Victim's stored Arguments and Justification are copied into the new request
The only control is the Exec ACL, checked for the caller on the same action

finding.guards_checked: The executor's stepACLCheck enforces Exec for the caller on that action. The Logs ACL (IsAllowedLogs, used by ExecutionStatus at api.go:468 and logEntryForAllowedViewer) is not applied. Compare siblings ExecutionStatus, GetActionLogs, GetLogs and KillAction, which all gate on ACL. Impact is limited to a caller who already has exec permission, so severity is low. They can re-run with the victim's argument values and justification without any visibility into them.
